searchText: We use BLST sha256 https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/master/src/asm/sha256-x86_64.pl That said people behind BLST are from OpenSSL and Intel crypto. Yeah those look like the respective codes in the Intel-ipsec-mb repo. I don't see the precomputed scheduled words for the padding block, so I think this is not optimized to hash just one block of 64 bytes Thanks! this worked, and my guess was right on target ``` 250.546, 0.000, 250.546, 250.546, 1, Compute Hash Tree Root of state ``` will move to lighthouse now, <@!539495253418180618> if you are around I'd really appreciate if you could tell me how to benchmark this on lighthouse It seems that lighthouse also uses supranational's blst code so probably is the same Alright, I posted the last I have here: https://hackmd.io/@potuz/rJX9iD30u Thanks and cc. <@!476250636548308992> <@!449019668296892420> <@!491624610215886849> <@!602753420033785856> and <@!340345049063882753> . I didn't manage to benchmark Teku without making the cache play in so that the second run was O(1) compared with the first one that matters. The results are there, I am not really sure if I traced correctly all implementations to supranational's blst cause all clients depend on that already for their BLS signing. But I think the result from this test shows that a simple addition to that library (or whatever library you are using) should increase hashing performance on all clients without them needing to change any code.

excerpts.author: mratsim
excerpts.content:
We use BLST sha256 https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/master/src/asm/sha256-x86_64.pl

That said people behind BLST are from OpenSSL and Intel crypto.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Yeah those look like the respective codes in the Intel-ipsec-mb repo. I don't see the precomputed scheduled words for the padding block, so I think this is not optimized to hash just one block of 64 bytes

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Thanks! this worked, and my guess was right on target 
```
     250.546,        0.000,      250.546,      250.546,            1, Compute Hash Tree Root of state
```
